Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like February 2020. The VIX is at 39, equities fell about 9% in one month, and long Treasuries rallied sharply. The 10-year yield is 1.30%, which fits late February, though that month ended near 1.15%. The fed funds rate is 1.58%, in line with early 2020.

Unemployment is 3.6%, and the data show a 12-month decline of 0.4 points. It was 3.5% in January 2020 and 3.5% in February, so 3.6% is slightly off. The 3.6% reading and the 10-year yield of 1.30% might fit March 2020 better, but fed funds would have dropped to about 0.65% by then. So that points back to February.

Other figures are consistent with February 2020. Headline CPI of 2.48% YoY is a bit high, but January 2020 was 2.5%. The snapshot may use data vintages as known at the time, so the unemployment figure may differ. Industrial production at -0.83% YoY also fits, and gold's 12-month return of 19.7% matches.

The 1-month equity drop of 9.3% fits February 2020, when the S&P 500 fell about 8.2%. Developed ex-US fell 9.4%, which also fits.

I pick February 2020.
